text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The centre-right Democratic Party admits it is reaping benefits from its cooperation in the government. More than 2,000 new members have registered with the party in the past three months.
- Illegal constructions are built by members of the public who seek permits for the buildings after they are completed.
- Sunday's anniversary to honour a Greek Cypriot and a Turkish Cypriot murdered in the 60s turned into a rally against chauvinism and nationalism.
- The United Nations suggest that the bicommunal dialogue (between Greek and Turkish Cypriots) start on guidelines set by former U.N. chief Boutros Boutros-Ghali.
- Difficulties remain in the ranks of opposition parties to field a common candidate in the presidential elections scheduled next year.

- Democratic Party leader Spyros Kyprianou warns President Glafcos Clerides he will withdraw his support for the government if there is a switch in policy on the Cyprus problem which his party does not agree with.
- President Clerides rules out a ban on military overflights with terms set by Ankara.
